To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the conformal Mellin representation is a powerful tool for NLO GPD analyses, (2) the NLO corrections to GPDs are small, and (3) the NLO correction to the DVMP cross section is large, but the NLO corrections are small in the kinematical region where the DVMP and DVMP data are available

(i) we provide a general formalism for NLO calculations in conformal space, (ii) we confirm previous findings for the pure singlet channel and (iii) we provide an estimate of higher-order corrections that suggests that NLO GPD extractions could be feasible.
the NLO corrections to DVCS and DVMP can be calculated in a straightforward way and that the resulting expressions can be used in a global fitting procedure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient and reliable fitting procedure to access GPDs from the experimental data of DVMP and DVMP.
the development and testing of the theoretical framework for a future NLO analysis of DVMP and DVMP+DVCS.
the development of the theoretical basis for global NLO GPDF fits to DVMP and DVMP data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a global fit to DVMP and DVMP data is feasible at the NLO level.
a NLO analysis of DVMP data is possible and that the results can be expected to provide a reliable description of the experimental data.
NLO effects in GPD analyses are not necessarily large, but that they should be included.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NLO corrections are under control, and that we can proceed to a global fit to GPDs.
the collinear factorisation approach to DVMP at NLO is under control and that a global NLO GPDF fit including DVMP is possible.
a global NLO analysis of DVMP data is feasible and can be done with a reasonable effort.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NLO calculations of GPDs from DVCS and DVMP data should not be too complicated to carry out.
a global GPD fit to DVCS and DVMP data can be carried out at NLO with a reasonable effort.
NLO corrections to DVMP are not as large as often feared, and that a global NLO GFD fit, combining DVCS and DVMP, should be feasible.
